# History

- `graph history <id> --json` lists how an entity changed, newest first:
  when, by which command, why, the names (not values) of what changed and
  the `tx_seq`. It shows who wrote a revision only as `own_session` (your
  session or not); who else did, only the maintainer can see.
- `graph get <id> --rev <value> --json` shows one earlier revision.
- A revision a pipeline wrote for a source (`graph apply` with `source`) has
  `source` (`name`, `version`, `run`); `graph changes` shows it per transaction.
- `graph changes --since tx:<seq> --json` (or a time, as for `--as-of`)
  lists what changed in the whole graph after a position, oldest first,
  names and ids only; continue with `next`.
- `--as-of tx:<seq>` on any read answers from the graph as it was after
  that transaction; just before a change is its `tx_seq` minus one. A
  time works too, with an offset (`2030-01-01T12:00:00Z`). Such answers
  carry the warning `temporal.as_of_read`.
- Earlier revisions are shown under the names of the current ontology:
  after a release that renamed a type, attribute or relation, `history`,
  `get --rev` and `--as-of` use the new names (with `--full`, such a
  revision has `names_mapped: true`), and queries name the new terms. An
  old name is unknown; the error says what it is called now.

## What the history holds, so entities do not

- A graph holds its subject: the things, their fields and relations. Put
  each fact into the field or relation the model has for it, and never
  repeat in a text field what a field or an edge already says.
- How you worked is not data: what you read and how (a page image, a text
  extraction), what you checked or left unchanged, a doubt, what is still
  to do. Say it in `--reason` (or `reason` of a change set) in English,
  whatever language the values are in; the history keeps it with the
  revision. Tell the user too. A gap you notice is
  closed (create the missing entity) or reported, not written into an
  entity.
- Who wrote a revision and when is in the history; write it into a field
  only when the model has one for it.
- Where the line runs depends on the graph: in a graph about documents,
  what a document says (a mark, a margin note, an error in it) is subject
  matter, how you read it is not. The graph's own skill names the line.
